statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Thursday’s persistent selloff remains a meaningful backdrop, but early post-reopen evidence is not sufficient to confirm renewed one-way Nasdaq extension.
recommendation: Tail remains just below the block threshold. The nearest concentration is the first post-reopen hours, followed by Friday U.S. cash-open and state-employment price discovery.
headline: Thursday selloff remains the risk backdrop; early Globex follow-through is not yet decisive.
body: The Nasdaq closed about 1% lower Thursday as Treasury yields rebounded and oil stayed elevated. Fresh shared context is healthy and shows seven of eight tracked megacaps negative, mixed semiconductor participation, and delayed NQ near flat after the reopen. Because independent post-reopen NQ bar evidence of repeated failed retracements is still insufficient, Tail is held at WATCH rather than block.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock hours, Tail moved from low overnight readings into repeated WATCH/BLOCK states during Thursday’s U.S. selloff, peaked at 29%, and eased to 27% after the close and first Globex reopening hour.
outlookSummary: Tail is modeled to decay overnight if futures remain two-sided. Friday’s U.S. cash-open and 16:00 Berlin state-employment release return the forecast to WATCH, with a secondary late-session and post-maintenance reopening checkpoint.

forecast.analysis: Thursday’s 1% Nasdaq decline remains the backdrop, but the fresh supporting feed shows delayed NQ near flat after Globex reopened. Independent post-reopen bar evidence is still insufficient to confirm another persistent one-way leg.

forecast.analysis: Overnight risk remains elevated but should decline if futures continue to rotate rather than extend Thursday’s selloff. A fresh yield or oil spike paired with NQ downside would keep Tail near WATCH.
This low-liquidity overnight hour carries residual continuation risk from Thursday’s close. Tail edges lower only if price discovery remains balanced and NQ does not hold near new session lows.

Tail remains at the lower edge of WATCH while the market digests Thursday’s risk-off close. Continued range development would reduce directional-efficiency risk; renewed extension would delay normalization.
By early European morning, an orderly overnight range would return Tail to the low band. Elevated oil and yields still keep Stress extreme even without evidence of mean-reversion failure.
Pre-Europe conditions are modeled as low Tail if overnight futures remain two-sided. Geopolitical and inflation-linked cross-asset stress persists, but no future directional move is assumed.
The European open can reprice global yields and oil. Tail stays low unless that cross-asset move aligns with renewed NQ extension; otherwise this hour remains a monitoring transition.
European price discovery may clarify whether Thursday’s selloff has broader follow-through. Tail stays low if NQ absorbs cross-asset moves with meaningful rotation rather than one-way extension.

U.S. premarket participation begins to matter more in this hour. Tail moves to WATCH conditionally because Thursday’s weak close can reassert itself as liquidity deepens, especially if yields and oil remain firm.
Premarket risk remains WATCH-level if the prior selloff is not clearly retraced. Balanced megacap and semiconductor participation would cap Tail; broad synchronized weakness would raise it.
Approaching the U.S. morning, Tail rises modestly as liquidity and directional conviction typically increase. The score remains below block without observed one-way structure.
The final pre-open hours carry higher conditional continuation risk after Thursday’s selloff. Tail remains WATCH unless futures show persistent extension with shallow or failed retracements.
Risk rises into the U.S. data/opening sequence. The scheduled state-employment release is a checkpoint rather than a directional assumption; Tail remains below block pending actual path evidence.

This hour contains the 15:30 Berlin U.S. cash open. Thursday’s weak close and extreme cross-asset Stress justify peak WATCH, but a block still requires observed opening continuation with poor retracement quality.
The 16:00 Berlin State Employment release overlaps early cash-session price discovery. Tail remains at 24% unless the observed post-release/opening path becomes persistently one-way.
After the first cash hour, Tail can ease if price discovery is orderly and retracements are meaningful. Continued extension after failed pullbacks would keep the score near or above the threshold.
Mid-morning risk is modeled slightly lower if the opening move loses directional efficiency. Oil, yields, megacaps and semiconductors remain the main cross-asset confirmation set.
Late-morning conditions are expected to become more two-sided absent a fresh catalyst. Tail stays WATCH because Thursday’s trend-down backdrop can still reassert itself.
Midday Tail remains at the lower WATCH boundary. A stable range and softer cross-asset pressure would support further decay; renewed synchronized downside would reverse that path.
Risk rises modestly into the U.S. power-hour transition. Late-day continuation is a conditional checkpoint after Thursday’s persistent weakness, not an assumed future trend.
The cash-close hour carries elevated continuation/reversal risk. Tail remains WATCH unless the observed late-day move becomes persistently directional with shallow pullbacks.
drivers: U.S. power hour and cash close

forecast.analysis: CME’s daily maintenance period removes continuous NQ price discovery. Tail falls mechanically toward the low-WATCH boundary because no new futures path can be observed, while headline Stress remains high.

Globex reopening after the maintenance break is a fresh price-discovery checkpoint. Tail returns to WATCH conditionally because Friday close positioning and geopolitical headlines can create a gap or renewed extension.

forecastDetail.comment: Current WATCH reflects Thursday’s persistent selloff plus extreme yields/oil stress, while post-reopen one-way NQ structure is not independently verified.
Tail eases conditionally if early Globex trade remains two-sided; renewed extension without meaningful retracement would invalidate the decay.
Overnight WATCH persists while yields and oil remain elevated; balanced futures rotation would reduce directional-efficiency risk.
Thin overnight liquidity keeps residual continuation risk, but Tail declines if NQ avoids holding near fresh lows.
The lower edge of WATCH assumes range development rather than renewed one-way extension from Thursday’s close.
Low Tail returns conditionally by early European morning if the overnight range remains orderly despite extreme background Stress.
